nex.scalar-field.note: A request that resolves one scalar. Dominated by parse, validation, and analysis rather than by execution.

nex.large-list.note: 2000 rows of six fields each: 14000 field resolutions. Measured near 7.3ms median on an idle machine, so the budget leaves room for a loaded one without hiding a regression.

nex.list-of-relations.note: 2000 rows behind a relation that has to be waited on. Rows resolve in windows rather than one after another, which is what keeps this from growing with the number of rows.

nex.paged-list.note: The same 2000 rows sorted and cut to 25. Only the page is completed, so this stays far below the whole list.

nex.loaded-list.note: The same 2000 rows behind a loader. Measured near 5.0ms median on an idle machine - below list-of-relations at 6.4ms, because 2000 asks are gathered into one call rather than awaited apart.

nex.directive-absent.note: A field carrying no directive, on a run that has directives configured. The baseline for what wrapping costs.

nex.directive-wrapped.note: The same request with one directive around the field. Both sit near 45us on an idle machine and the medians match, so this holds the claim that a directive costs the field it wraps and nothing else. The baseline is well above the 5us floor, so the ratio here is measuring the code rather than the machine.
